approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent molecular-string prior on the original unlabeled corpus, then chooses its published checkpoint by valid, connected, distinct ancestral emissions on a fixed sampling probe, with heldout string loss breaking ties. Each objective starts a fresh adaptable flow policy beside that frozen reference. Accepted trajectories train the policy through trajectory balance and score-ranked replay. A neural batch alternates with two graph batches: accepted neural molecules refresh a score-ranked breeding population, and the first graph handoff protects a real descendant of a fresh neural parent. Fragment crossover and seven atom/bond mutations generate temporary offspring pools. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior fitted only to accepted scores chooses the other graph evaluations by correlated function draws. Accepted graph descendants can survive for breeding and train the neural policy. Its bond-change mutation currently changes bond order; it has no explicit operation for moving an intact substituent to an adjacent aromatic position.
approach.novelty: Add intact acyclic branch relocation to the existing bond-change menu. An attached group can move from an aromatic carbon to a neighboring aromatic carbon bearing hydrogen while retaining every atom, the complete branch and the ring framework. This exposes substitution-position alternatives without first deleting or replacing the group. It is new to this reciprocal lineage: its previous graph sibling restricted crossover attachments and nearly eliminated evaluated crossovers. A separate graph-walk lineage already demonstrated the relocation operation, but none of its ten evaluated moves won a batch. The new question is whether the Parent's surplus offspring pools and unchanged posterior selection can make useful evaluated descendants from that structural channel.

hypothesis: Extend the existing graph change_bond menu with relocation of an intact single-attachment acyclic branch from an aromatic carbon to its adjacent hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon, preserving the branch, ring framework and molecular formula while exposing positional isomers to the unchanged offspring posterior.

finding_summary.headline: Relocations yield retained improvements, with a small and uneven panel gain
finding_summary.insights:
The earlier graph-walk transfer case left useful retention unresolved: ten moves were evaluated, only one improved its source, and none was retained for a later walk. The reciprocal optimizer now demonstrates that positional alternatives can improve real molecules and enter both breeding and neural replay. The four improvements from a single relocation provide the clearest local evidence, including a fluorine move that gains 0.033311 and an ether-group move that gains 0.139485. Three task/seed terminal winners have graph ancestry through accepted relocations. This narrows the question from whether the channel can be used to when its limited evaluation allocation is worthwhile.

Selection remains a substantial filter: 172 of the 187 admitted positional alternatives were unselected and have no measured scores. Every legacy bond-order choice on an expanded menu failed sanitization, so the added options provide valid exits from otherwise failing bond choices, but they also change subsequent retries and random trajectories. The small panel gain therefore cannot be assigned wholly to the successful relocations. The largest task gain is in sitagliptin, where neither evaluated relocation improved its source and the terminal winners have no recorded graph ancestry through a relocation. Indirect effects through replay and altered search allocation remain possible. The poorer overall graph yield and opposing seed effects limit any claim of a broad efficiency improvement.

The molecular assessment supports a placement question within already abundant aromatic, amine and carbonyl chemistry. Conserving an existing group does not make that group chemically conventional: unusual nitrogen, sulfur, peroxide and strained-ring motifs, along with unspecified stereochemistry, remain in the generated molecules. Formula and core preservation establish the intended graph edit, while synthesis and stability remain outside the measured result. A separate inherited identity issue also persists in a few unselected legacy pool products; it caused no emitted-proposal or feedback failure in this panel.
finding_summary.results:
All 191 sampled relocations preserved the complete branch, ring framework, atom attributes and molecular formula. Of these, 190 changed molecular identity and 187 became novel, encodable positional alternatives. The optimizer evaluated 15: 13 selected from ordinary pools and two protected descendants. Four of the 11 single relocations without crossover improved their scored source; one of four crossover-plus-relocation descendants beat its best generating parent. All 15 entered replay, and 14 were later used for breeding. Their later direct descendants received 64 evaluations, although only one of those 64 beat its best parent. This establishes evaluated and retained structural contribution beyond temporary pool access.

The complete three-seed panel mean rose from 0.550198 to 0.553056. The paired gain of 0.002859 exceeds the registered 0.002 minimum, but seed changes were +0.011491, -0.048498 and +0.045583. Sitagliptin and zaleplon task means rose by 0.107257 and 0.007994; deco hop, median and DRD2 fell by 0.078129, 0.019214 and 0.003614. Overall graph parent-beating yield declined from 452 to 440 of 2,850 evaluations, or 15.86% to 15.44%. Every task completed its budget, every pool filled, and all 150 protected handoffs preserved accepted neural-parent provenance.

molecular.headline: Aromatic polycycles and amine-rich ligands coexist with N-fluoro heterocycles, strained cages and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives and seeds 0, 1 and 2 were read in full for this node and Parent n-dd7b8aa31113: each task has 900 trajectory rows, including 870 optimizer proposals. There are no tasks without trajectories. The digest final excerpts cover the end of seed 2; they are not a summary of the other seeds or a list of retained best molecules. This is an abundant ring-producing generator. In the fixed task order, the digest ring-closure rates are 0.9851, 0.9931, 0.9885, 0.9931 and 0.9943, and aromatic-presence rates are 0.9724, 0.9851, 0.9736, 0.9793 and 0.9506. These are fractions of optimizer SMILES containing the relevant text, not fractions of atoms or a ring-perception result. The corresponding mean SMILES lengths are 44.2, 66.5, 49.9, 57.2 and 45.8. RDKit readings of the complete optimizer trajectories give median heavy-atom counts 25, 35, 28, 32 and 25. Every optimizer row parses in the available RDKit environment, but that is not evidence of a practical synthesis. There is broad chemistry across seeds: fused aza-aromatics with amides, hydrazones, linked sulfonamide/heteroaryl systems, aryl-substituted tertiary amines, indole-fused lactams and fluorinated nitrogen-rich rings. Upper-score neighborhoods often repeat one such family. Ordinary medicinal motifs coexist with N-F, peroxide, sulfenamide, unusual sulfur-valence and small-ring products. Stereocentre text rates are 0.0 on every task; full-trajectory RDKit readings find unassigned tetrahedral centres in 254, 193, 484, 379 and 398 optimizer rows in the fixed task order, with no assigned tetrahedral centres. Parent comparisons below describe changed chemical families alongside their recorded scores; they do not establish which algorithmic operation caused an outcome. All size, ring and bond-motif counts are structural readings of the supplied molecules. No new objective score or synthesis score was computed.

per_task.generated_character: The upper digest is unusually consistent in molecular size: its molecules have 24 or 25 heavy atoms, usually a fused bicyclic aromatic domain plus another ring. Seed 1 reaches a partially saturated fused aza-ring system bearing an N-methyl carboxamide, N-methyl aromatic nitrogen and fluorophenyl group (0.4956786237874378). Seed 0 instead reaches an aza-aromatic/quinoline-type pair joined by an imine, with a terminal alkene, alcohol and hydroxy heteroaromatic group (0.4552001836634155). Seed 2 reaches naphthyl hydrazones of an amide-bearing carbon centre, with a hydroxyphenyl amide and sometimes an aryl thiol (0.4455495560238204). These include recognizable synthetic motifs, although the imine/hydrazone and N-hydroxy variants introduce chemical and configurational uncertainty. Parent best molecules also had 25 heavy atoms, but included an unusual sulfur-containing fused heteroaromatic, an N-amino fused aromatic carboxamide, and a nitrile-bearing partly saturated aza-ring carboxamide. The corresponding Parent seed best scores were 0.49151859442707624, 0.4163503402962837 and 0.46457806514522626. The child changes the functional-group arrangements within the same compact aromatic size regime; it does not reveal a shortage of rings.
liabilities: Hydrazones and imines introduce possible hydrolysis, tautomer and geometrical-isomer concerns; phenolic and thiol substituents add potential oxidation liabilities. Their actual stability has not been measured.

The N-hydroxy aromatic analogue and the O-S-containing alcohol-side-chain analogue are less routine medicinal structures than the corresponding amide/ether motifs, despite scores of 0.4624615253670981 and 0.4319502594615478.
Some proposals discard molecular scale entirely, producing water or oversized assemblies that lose the useful compact arrangement.
missing_features: The upper child families do not reproduce the Parent's favorable combination of nitrile and carboxamide on a compact aza-ring framework. Nitrile-containing optimizer rows fall from 110 in the Parent to 25 in the child; nitriles are underrepresented here, not globally absent, and this does not prove that adding a nitrile to a current molecule would help.

Coverage of chemically conventional alternatives preserving the observed carbonyl, aromatic-nitrogen and donor relationships is uneven: leading neighborhoods also use hydrazones, an N-hydroxy heterocycle and an O-S-containing side chain.
The fused carboxamide centre and the imine/hydrazone geometries are not specified stereochemically. The observations establish missing specification, not a measured preference for a configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Compact, connected aromatic structures with appropriately situated nitrogen/oxygen functionality separate the upper molecules from both extremes. Water scores 0.0, while the cited 50-heavy-atom multiaryl/polyamine assembly scores 6.15474583885519e-39. A standard methoxy-substituted indole carboxamide in the initial observations already scores 0.3051048083696145. Within the hydrazone family, the unthiolated naphthyl compound scores 0.44320263021395917 and its thiol-bearing relative 0.4455495560238204; adding another fluorine gives 0.4201182934804424. A final relative combining carbonyl removal with phenyl-to-aza-aryl substitution gives 0.38723016207970795; those simultaneous changes cannot be assigned separate effects. Partial saturation of the naphthyl domain gives 0.31263939498209775. These local contrasts support sensitivity to carbonyl placement and ring electronics, rather than a general reward for more sulfur, halogen or aromatic bulk. They do not identify one required missing pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The generator explores the largest molecular scale of this panel: optimizer heavy-atom counts span 1 to 102 with a median of 35. Seed 0 upper molecules are heavily aromatic sulfonamides organized around adjacent-nitrogen heteroaromatic rings, fused oxazole-containing groups and either aryl carbonyls or large halogenated biaryl branches. The best example has 38 heavy atoms and five aromatic rings (0.6106504275719098); a near-tied chlorinated/trifluoromethylated example has 48 heavy atoms and six aromatic rings (0.6097370766488414). Seed 1 instead reaches a much more compact 25-heavy-atom cyano/fluorothiophene thioamide linked to aza/sulfur heteroaromatics (0.6079884633442887). Seed 2 uses nitroimidazole/triazole and other nitrogen-rich linked rings, ending with cationic and strained fused-ring derivatives; its best is 0.5964680744092509. These are distinct families, not a single collapsed scaffold. The Parent seed 1 upper family contained linked quinazoline-type systems and a carbonylated piperazine, with additional unusual sulfur/nitrogen functionality, and reached 0.8301591128254581. That chemical arrangement is not represented by the child's leading sulfonamide/thioamide families. Parent seed 0 and seed 2 best scores were 0.6039553752535497 and 0.6153794851273843, so the chemistry/score comparison differs substantially by seed.
liabilities: The highly halogenated multiaryl branch carries substantial aromatic and halogen burden, while the compact sulfur-rich family introduces thioamide and multiple sulfur heterocycles. Practical solubility, metabolic behavior and synthetic routes remain unknown.
The terminal-sulfur replacement of a sulfonyl oxygen and the seed 2 cationic nitrogen-oxygen/fused-small-ring structures are chemically less routine despite favorable recorded scores.

The final undercoordinated nitrogen-cation structure scores 0.5693448110951698 and is assigned four radical electrons by RDKit. The digest charged-text rate of 0.1943 also includes ordinary nitro representations; charge notation alone should not be treated as the liability.
missing_features: The high child excerpts lack the Parent's particularly favorable fused aza-ring/carbonylated cyclic-amine arrangement. This supports a gap in coverage of alternative core/linker relationships, not a prescription to copy its unusual nitroso/sulfur decoration.

The leading families show little separation between conventional sulfonamide chemistry and less routine sulfur-valence replacements. Chemically credible alternatives retaining the same polar attachment geometry are incompletely represented.

The upper seed 2 family lacks a consistently ordinary closed-shell, low-strain realization of its linked nitrogen-rich rings. Its score does not establish that adding more charged nitrogen or more fused rings is useful.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The visible gradient favors specific connected heteroaromatic arrangements over merely having sulfonamide, amide and aryl groups somewhere in a molecule. The cited sulfone/amide/sulfonamide chain scores 0.29444616217051867, an aromatic acid/ester/acylsulfone arrangement scores 0.298374613003096, and the 53-heavy-atom acid-containing assembly scores 0.28988718775181305. Both compact thioamide and larger sulfonamide upper molecules exceed those examples, so neither simple size minimization nor total aromatic count explains the ordering. Extending the compact thiophene thioamide with another fluorothiophene changes the score only from 0.6079884633442887 to 0.6078616701879239. Replacing a sulfonyl oxygen by terminal sulfur leaves the quoted large molecule at exactly 0.6097370766488414. The observed objective is therefore not reliably discriminating the chemical plausibility of these closely related sulfur environments.

per_task.generated_character: The recognizable shared feature of the successful molecules is an accessible non-amide aliphatic amine joined to hydrophobic aromatic domains. The optimizer median is 28 heavy atoms. Seed 0 reaches flexible amide-linked polyamine/aryl compounds (best 0.9871033448480295), seed 1 a tertiary aralkyl amine with a phenol and a fused hydrocarbon domain (0.9895333802040542), and seed 2 both diaryl-ether/piperidine families and extensively bridged ether/aryl/piperidine structures. The best cited molecule has 27 heavy atoms, a tertiary piperidine nitrogen, aryl ethers, a carbon-bound fluorine, an N-cyclopropenylmethyl substituent and small cycles within the bridged aromatic framework (0.9999898280394668). Less cage-like diaryl ethers with a piperidine and an aminoalkenyl side chain already reach 0.9905431868120467. Parent best chemistry likewise ranged from bridged amines to long-linker arylpiperazines, with seed best scores 0.98747470209114, 0.9999943278368041 and 0.9999999657062248. The child preserves the broad amine/aromatic relationship but changes the scaffolds, linker geometry and small-ring burden.
liabilities: The upper examples contain cyclopropene or azetine appendages and small cycles embedded in bridged aryl frameworks. These are substantial ring-strain and synthesis concerns even though the graphs parse.
Chloromethyl and chloroethyl tertiary-amine substituents are potential reactive liabilities; their high objective values cannot be read as stability measurements.

Hydrophobic polyaryl and halogenated domains, multiple amines in some families, and unspecified stereochemistry complicate medicinal interpretation. Some later products additionally contain peroxide bonds.
missing_features: There is no evidence that the generator is missing basic amine centres or aromatic domains: both are already plentiful in its successful output. The practical gap in the leading cage family is coverage of comparably organized amine/aromatic arrangements with more conventional ring geometry.

Defined configurations at the bridged and substituted saturated centres are absent, and the aminoalkene geometry is unspecified. No score benefit from choosing a stereoisomer is established by these data.

The strongest local neighborhood offers insufficient evidence that its amine placement can be preserved while replacing haloalkyl, peroxide or highly strained unsaturated-ring attachments with more routine functional groups.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Amine environment matters more than simply counting nitrogen. The acyl/sulfonyl-blocked nitrogen compound scores 3.8021829379963674e-05, the nitroaryl acylhydrazone 4.1105044111594925e-05, and the N-acyl seven-membered amine 0.00021594328729095667. These already contain rings and nitrogen, but lack the freely available aliphatic amine context of the high families. The high-score region also tolerates concerning features: chloromethyl and chloroethyl amines score 0.9922758515684804 and 0.9936059985092686, while brominated and fluorinated small-unsaturated-ring analogues both score 0.9999811926223046. A peroxide-bearing cyclic derivative still gives 0.914606268793902. The gradient supports amine/aromatic placement; it does not independently establish affinity, selectivity, a safe haloalkyl group, or the practical feasibility of the top cages.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer median is 32 heavy atoms, and the upper molecules combine aromatic domains with cyclic carbonyl/nitrogen functionality. Seed 2 concentrates on an indole-fused pyridone/lactam attached to a methylenedioxyaryl group, with ethoxy and propoxy substituents. The best cited structures each have 30 heavy atoms, five perceived rings and four aromatic rings (0.2337783943190832). The conventional directly connected aryl/lactam family is synthetically more recognizable than its N-S-linked, peroxide or O-S-substituted derivatives. Seed 0 reaches a partly saturated fused cyclic carbonyl system bearing a sulfonyl morpholine and aryl/aza-aryl groups (0.21643049217277108); seed 1 reaches a fused carbonylated nitrogen heterocycle with substituted aryl groups (0.20829364701364125). The Parent also sampled cyclic carbonyl/aryl families, but its strongest seed 1 molecule used a diazepinone-like core and sulfonylpiperazine arrangement at 0.26493557493264663. Parent seed 0 and seed 2 best scores were 0.21407396945703827 and 0.2371358719187444. The child's different upper scaffolds do not demonstrate more complete coverage of those useful carbonyl/amine relationships.
liabilities: The core indole/lactam and methylenedioxyaryl chemistry is recognizable, but some neighboring proposals replace ordinary connections with sulfenamides, peroxides or sulfenate-like groups.
A final truncated indole-fused lactam bears an N-O-F attachment and scores 0.17020114957538862; that attachment is not an ordinary medicinal substitute for the missing aryl domain.
Repeated whole aromatic/lactam units create large, crowded structures without preserving the favorable score. Tiny fragments and long ring-free polyenes also appear at the opposite size extreme.
missing_features: The leading family incompletely covers alternative cyclic carbonyl, aza-ring and cyclic-amine arrangements exemplified by the better-scoring Parent family. The output does not establish a single required absent group or prove that more rings would improve the objective.

Functionality-preserving alternatives to N-S, O-O and N-O-F attachment chemistry are unevenly explored within the upper neighborhoods, even though a conventional aryl/lactam connection already scores well.
Specified stereochemistry is absent in the partly saturated fused-ring families; this is a representation and synthetic-definition gap rather than an observed stereochemical score gradient.

Local alkoxy changes are modest: the diethoxy relative scores 0.23091541216087028, and the two quoted ethoxy/propoxy attachment variants share 0.2337783943190832. An N-S-linked relative scores 0.22644622562118344; another N-S-linked derivative and an aryl peroxide both score 0.22582153143093536. The close scores of conventional and reactive-bond variants do not establish that the latter chemistry is beneficial.

Seed 2 mainly produces a conjugated nine-membered nitrogen-rich ring carrying carbonyl or imino groups, N-methyl substituents, an N-fluoropyrrole and a fluorinated cyclopentadienol. The best molecule has 27 heavy atoms and perceived ring sizes 5, 5 and 9 (0.5939062829029609); this should not be described as an ordinary six-membered pyrimidinedione simply because it has two carbonyls and N-methyl groups. Other upper structures fluorinate another ring nitrogen or contract the unsaturated carbocycle. Seed 0 instead reaches a fluorinated pyridyl ether/sulfonamide joined to a nitrogen-rich saturated small ring with an N-F bond and a cycloheptadienyl group (0.49998781221131255). Seed 1 reaches a more recognizable carbon-fluorinated urea/imidazole-containing molecule at 0.35528710288824195. The Parent upper molecules were compact fluorinated N/O or sulfur-containing ring systems, with seed best scores 0.4148943261002915, 0.3878327786264519 and 0.3246833344580741. The child's stronger recorded fluorinated families coincide with a substantial chemical shift: 160 of its 870 optimizer molecules contain an N-F bond, compared with 5 in the Parent. This is a bond-connectivity count, not a claim that fluorination itself caused a score increase.
liabilities: All of the best digest molecules carry at least one N-F bond. N-fluoropyrroles and fluorinated ring nitrogens are unusual medicinal attachments and raise reactivity and synthesis questions that the objective does not resolve.

The nine-membered conjugated nitrogen-rich ring, cyclopentadienol and contracted unsaturated-ring analogues raise ring-geometry and tautomer-definition concerns. RDKit aromaticity and valence acceptance are insufficient evidence of stable, isolable structures.
Repeated heterocyclic assemblies and long alkyl tails can destroy the compact molecular arrangement, while a higher score in a chemically unusual family does not establish better drug-likeness.
missing_features: The leading family lacks a demonstrated conventional medicinal scaffold reproducing its nitrogen/oxygen/fluorine arrangement without the N-fluoropyrrole and expanded conjugated ring. Ordinary carbon-fluorinated polar chemistry is accessible elsewhere in the same trajectory, but equivalent upper scores for such replacements are not shown.

Controlled ring-size and saturation alternatives preserving the favorable local arrangement are incompletely covered. The generator reaches both nine-membered conjugated heterocycles and contracted unsaturated carbocycles, without evidence that those geometries are practically realizable.

The fluorinated saturated carbons and other configurationally rich centres remain unspecified. The supplied scores do not establish a missing primary amine, a required reference scaffold or a preferred stereoisomer.

The fluorinated nine-membered dicarbonyl structure scores 0.5939062829029609; a related carbonyl/imino isomer scores 0.5897228332591999, and a less fluorinated carbonyl/imino relative 0.5073549274003079. A fused five/six-membered dicarbonyl analogue scores 0.4721809545982841, and the hydroxyphenyl-substituted nine-membered relative 0.46490923907729875. Conversely, a close hydroxylated aromatic derivative gives 0.11054598243422825, and hydroxylation of the N-fluoropyrrole in a contracted-ring relative gives 0.017397599952024095. Duplicating the nitrogen-rich heterocyclic motif into a 45-heavy-atom assembly gives 1.0688952839873028e-08; the long-alkyl-tail compound scores 0.0 and the large polyfunctional sulfur/polyol assembly 3.3014463410386146e-105. They do not support indiscriminate fluorination, adding polar groups, or assigning a biological rationale to N-F bonds.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A large sulfonamide and the analogue replacing one sulfonyl oxygen by terminal sulfur share 0.6097370766488414. A peroxide and an N-S-linked lactam derivative share 0.22582153143093536. Another upper family contains N-F bonds in every best-digest molecule, and its full trajectory has 160 N-F-containing optimizer rows versus 5 in the corresponding Parent trajectory. A final undercoordinated nitrogen-cation molecule has a recorded score of 0.5693448110951698 despite RDKit assigning radical electrons. Ordinary ethers, amides, sulfonamides and carbon-bound fluorine are also present, so this is inconsistent chemical context rather than inability to make those groups.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve ordinary functional-group chemistry while exploring favorable local arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support alternative connections and atom environments that retain a useful donor, acceptor, amine or halogen relationship without requiring a peroxide, undercoordinated charged centre, unusual sulfur valence or N-F attachment. Distinguish amine, amide, heteroaromatic nitrogen, sulfonamide and sulfenamide environments instead of treating element identity or graph sanitization as equivalent chemistry. Any value of the alternatives must come from current-session accepted feedback; the observations do not justify a universal ban on nitrogen, sulfur, fluorine or formal charge.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest stereocentre rate is 0.0. Full optimizer trajectories contain 254, 193, 484, 379 and 398 rows with unassigned tetrahedral centres in the brief's fixed task order, with none assigned. The cited structures include fused saturated carboxamides, bridged tertiary amines, fluorinated carbocycles, cyclopropene or azetine appendages, and a nine-membered conjugated nitrogen-rich ring. Some highly scoring bridged aromatic frameworks contain small perceived cycles.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit stereochemical definition and controlled ring geometry are missing from configurationally rich output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide access to defined configurations and chemically credible ring-size, saturation and bridge alternatives around accepted arrangements. Preserve existing stereochemical information during changes that do not require its removal, and keep configuration changes distinguishable from connectivity changes. A valid ring closure or additional aromatic text should not stand in for realistic geometry; these data do not establish a preferred stereoisomer or guarantee a score benefit from reducing strain.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied low examples include water, a small nitrile/amidoxime fragment, a long ring-free polyene and a long-alkyl-tail structure. A repeated aromatic/lactam assembly gives 0.17336672809095632 where a compact related arrangement gives 0.2337783943190832; duplication of a nitrogen-rich heterocyclic motif gives 1.0688952839873028e-08 where a compact family member gives 0.5939062829029609. Conversely, useful linked aromatic structures occur at both 25 and 48 heavy atoms with scores 0.6079884633442887 and 0.6097370766488414, ruling out a single universally favorable molecular size.
transferable_gaps.gap: Growth and contraction can lose coherent molecular scale by repeating whole motifs or removing the core.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable incremental growth, contraction and linker replacement that retain a connected core and its observed functional-group relationships. Supply alternatives to whole-motif multiplication and severe fragmentation, letting accepted local observations determine suitable scale instead of imposing a fixed size target or assuming that adding another favorable fragment transfers its value.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The complete panel contains distinct fused aza-amide, hydrazone, linked heteroaryl/sulfonamide, thioamide, arylamine and lactam families, yet the upper excerpts concentrate on repeated local structures. A nitrile/carboxamide arrangement favorable in the Parent is absent from the corresponding child upper excerpt, while nitrile-containing rows decrease from 110 to 25. A different Parent cyclic carbonyl/amine arrangement scores 0.26493557493264663, above the child's alternative upper family at 0.2337783943190832. Within the child, a carbonyl-containing hydrazone gives 0.4455495560238204 while a relative combining carbonyl removal and an additional aromatic nitrogen gives 0.38723016207970795; the individual changes are not isolated. In another family, peripheral alkoxy attachment alternatives tie at 0.2337783943190832. These are evidence for uneven chemical relationship coverage, not proof of absent positional access or of any particular operator's effect.
transferable_gaps.gap: Coverage of distinct useful cores and their functional-group relationships remains uneven within leading families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain access to chemically distinct cores present in the current accepted observations and explore core/linker alternatives that preserve useful local donor, acceptor and accessible-amine relationships. Treat replacing a group, moving its attachment, changing its electronic environment and exchanging the supporting scaffold as different chemical questions. Broader strings or more ring closures alone do not demonstrate coverage of those relationships, and neither prior-task labels nor a fixed molecule library is required to express this generative capability.

method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

finding_summary.headline: Relocations yield retained improvements, with a small and uneven panel gain
finding_summary.insights:
The earlier graph-walk transfer case left useful retention unresolved: ten moves were evaluated, only one improved its source, and none was retained for a later walk. The reciprocal optimizer now demonstrates that positional alternatives can improve real molecules and enter both breeding and neural replay. The four improvements from a single relocation provide the clearest local evidence, including a fluorine move that gains 0.033311 and an ether-group move that gains 0.139485. Three task/seed terminal winners have graph ancestry through accepted relocations. This narrows the question from whether the channel can be used to when its limited evaluation allocation is worthwhile.

Selection remains a substantial filter: 172 of the 187 admitted positional alternatives were unselected and have no measured scores. Every legacy bond-order choice on an expanded menu failed sanitization, so the added options provide valid exits from otherwise failing bond choices, but they also change subsequent retries and random trajectories. The small panel gain therefore cannot be assigned wholly to the successful relocations. The largest task gain is in sitagliptin, where neither evaluated relocation improved its source and the terminal winners have no recorded graph ancestry through a relocation. Indirect effects through replay and altered search allocation remain possible. The poorer overall graph yield and opposing seed effects limit any claim of a broad efficiency improvement.

The molecular assessment supports a placement question within already abundant aromatic, amine and carbonyl chemistry. Conserving an existing group does not make that group chemically conventional: unusual nitrogen, sulfur, peroxide and strained-ring motifs, along with unspecified stereochemistry, remain in the generated molecules. Formula and core preservation establish the intended graph edit, while synthesis and stability remain outside the measured result. A separate inherited identity issue also persists in a few unselected legacy pool products; it caused no emitted-proposal or feedback failure in this panel.

finding_summary.headline: Relocations yield retained improvements, with a small and uneven panel gain
finding_summary.insights:
The earlier graph-walk transfer case left useful retention unresolved: ten moves were evaluated, only one improved its source, and none was retained for a later walk. The reciprocal optimizer now demonstrates that positional alternatives can improve real molecules and enter both breeding and neural replay. The four improvements from a single relocation provide the clearest local evidence, including a fluorine move that gains 0.033311 and an ether-group move that gains 0.139485. Three task/seed terminal winners have graph ancestry through accepted relocations. This narrows the question from whether the channel can be used to when its limited evaluation allocation is worthwhile.

Selection remains a substantial filter: 172 of the 187 admitted positional alternatives were unselected and have no measured scores. Every legacy bond-order choice on an expanded menu failed sanitization, so the added options provide valid exits from otherwise failing bond choices, but they also change subsequent retries and random trajectories. The small panel gain therefore cannot be assigned wholly to the successful relocations. The largest task gain is in sitagliptin, where neither evaluated relocation improved its source and the terminal winners have no recorded graph ancestry through a relocation. Indirect effects through replay and altered search allocation remain possible. The poorer overall graph yield and opposing seed effects limit any claim of a broad efficiency improvement.

The molecular assessment supports a placement question within already abundant aromatic, amine and carbonyl chemistry. Conserving an existing group does not make that group chemically conventional: unusual nitrogen, sulfur, peroxide and strained-ring motifs, along with unspecified stereochemistry, remain in the generated molecules. Formula and core preservation establish the intended graph edit, while synthesis and stability remain outside the measured result. A separate inherited identity issue also persists in a few unselected legacy pool products; it caused no emitted-proposal or feedback failure in this panel.

finding_summary.headline: Relocations yield retained improvements, with a small and uneven panel gain
finding_summary.insights:
The earlier graph-walk transfer case left useful retention unresolved: ten moves were evaluated, only one improved its source, and none was retained for a later walk. The reciprocal optimizer now demonstrates that positional alternatives can improve real molecules and enter both breeding and neural replay. The four improvements from a single relocation provide the clearest local evidence, including a fluorine move that gains 0.033311 and an ether-group move that gains 0.139485. Three task/seed terminal winners have graph ancestry through accepted relocations. This narrows the question from whether the channel can be used to when its limited evaluation allocation is worthwhile.

Selection remains a substantial filter: 172 of the 187 admitted positional alternatives were unselected and have no measured scores. Every legacy bond-order choice on an expanded menu failed sanitization, so the added options provide valid exits from otherwise failing bond choices, but they also change subsequent retries and random trajectories. The small panel gain therefore cannot be assigned wholly to the successful relocations. The largest task gain is in sitagliptin, where neither evaluated relocation improved its source and the terminal winners have no recorded graph ancestry through a relocation. Indirect effects through replay and altered search allocation remain possible. The poorer overall graph yield and opposing seed effects limit any claim of a broad efficiency improvement.

The molecular assessment supports a placement question within already abundant aromatic, amine and carbonyl chemistry. Conserving an existing group does not make that group chemically conventional: unusual nitrogen, sulfur, peroxide and strained-ring motifs, along with unspecified stereochemistry, remain in the generated molecules. Formula and core preservation establish the intended graph edit, while synthesis and stability remain outside the measured result. A separate inherited identity issue also persists in a few unselected legacy pool products; it caused no emitted-proposal or feedback failure in this panel.

molecular_assessment.overall_character: All five objectives and seeds 0, 1 and 2 were read in full for this node and Parent n-dd7b8aa31113: each task has 900 trajectory rows, including 870 optimizer proposals. RDKit readings of the complete optimizer trajectories give median heavy-atom counts 25, 35, 28, 32 and 25. Every optimizer row parses in the available RDKit environment, but that is not evidence of a practical synthesis. There is broad chemistry across seeds: fused aza-aromatics with amides, hydrazones, linked sulfonamide/heteroaryl systems, aryl-substituted tertiary amines, indole-fused lactams and fluorinated nitrogen-rich rings. Upper-score neighborhoods often repeat one such family. Ordinary medicinal motifs coexist with N-F, peroxide, sulfenamide, unusual sulfur-valence and small-ring products. Stereocentre text rates are 0.0 on every task; full-trajectory RDKit readings find unassigned tetrahedral centres in 254, 193, 484, 379 and 398 optimizer rows in the fixed task order, with no assigned tetrahedral centres. Parent comparisons below describe changed chemical families alongside their recorded scores; they do not establish which algorithmic operation caused an outcome. All size, ring and bond-motif counts are structural readings of the supplied molecules. No new objective score or synthesis score was computed.

per_task.generated_character: The upper digest is unusually consistent in molecular size: its molecules have 24 or 25 heavy atoms, usually a fused bicyclic aromatic domain plus another ring. Seed 1 reaches a partially saturated fused aza-ring system bearing an N-methyl carboxamide, N-methyl aromatic nitrogen and fluorophenyl group (0.4956786237874378). Seed 0 instead reaches an aza-aromatic/quinoline-type pair joined by an imine, with a terminal alkene, alcohol and hydroxy heteroaromatic group (0.4552001836634155). Seed 2 reaches naphthyl hydrazones of an amide-bearing carbon centre, with a hydroxyphenyl amide and sometimes an aryl thiol (0.4455495560238204). These include recognizable synthetic motifs, although the imine/hydrazone and N-hydroxy variants introduce chemical and configurational uncertainty. Parent best molecules also had 25 heavy atoms, but included an unusual sulfur-containing fused heteroaromatic, an N-amino fused aromatic carboxamide, and a nitrile-bearing partly saturated aza-ring carboxamide. The corresponding Parent seed best scores were 0.49151859442707624, 0.4163503402962837 and 0.46457806514522626. The child changes the functional-group arrangements within the same compact aromatic size regime; it does not reveal a shortage of rings.
liabilities: Hydrazones and imines introduce possible hydrolysis, tautomer and geometrical-isomer concerns; phenolic and thiol substituents add potential oxidation liabilities. Their actual stability has not been measured.

The N-hydroxy aromatic analogue and the O-S-containing alcohol-side-chain analogue are less routine medicinal structures than the corresponding amide/ether motifs, despite scores of 0.4624615253670981 and 0.4319502594615478.
Some proposals discard molecular scale entirely, producing water or oversized assemblies that lose the useful compact arrangement.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent molecular-string prior on the original unlabeled corpus, then chooses its published checkpoint by valid, connected, distinct ancestral emissions on a fixed sampling probe, with heldout string loss breaking ties. Each objective starts a fresh adaptable flow policy beside that frozen reference. Accepted trajectories train the policy through trajectory balance and score-ranked replay. A neural batch alternates with two graph batches: accepted neural molecules refresh a score-ranked breeding population, and the first graph handoff protects a real descendant of a fresh neural parent. Fragment crossover and seven atom/bond mutations generate temporary offspring pools. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior fitted only to accepted scores chooses the other graph evaluations by correlated function draws. Accepted graph descendants can survive for breeding and train the neural policy. Its bond-change mutation currently changes bond order; it has no explicit operation for moving an intact substituent to an adjacent aromatic position.
approach.novelty: Add intact acyclic branch relocation to the existing bond-change menu. An attached group can move from an aromatic carbon to a neighboring aromatic carbon bearing hydrogen while retaining every atom, the complete branch and the ring framework. This exposes substitution-position alternatives without first deleting or replacing the group. It is new to this reciprocal lineage: its previous graph sibling restricted crossover attachments and nearly eliminated evaluated crossovers. A separate graph-walk lineage already demonstrated the relocation operation, but none of its ten evaluated moves won a batch. The new question is whether the Parent's surplus offspring pools and unchanged posterior selection can make useful evaluated descendants from that structural channel.
